newsitem.title: USA: SyStemix stem cell mixture engrafts rapidly.
newsitem.headline: SyStemix stem cell mixture engrafts rapidly.

text.p: SyStemix Inc said its hematopoietic stem cell transplant mixture has been shown to engraft in cancer chemotherapy patients in less than two weeks, about the same amount of time as less concentrated mixtures that are currently used.
Hematopoietic stem cells are the "mother cells" that regenerate to form all of the blood and immune system. SyStemix has a patented system to separate these cells from other types of blood cells.

"Previously it was thought that this more powerful subset of cells would take a longer time to engraft in a patient," said SyStemix Chief Financial Officer Wendy Hitchcodk. "But our data showed no delay at all. These are pure, disease-free, wonderful cells."

Bone marrow transplants are commonly used to prevent infection and bleeding following high-dose chemotherapy treatment. The less concentrated transplants currently used include more peripheral cells and may contain some cancerous cells as well.
The results reported Tuesday are from European Phase I/II clinical trials. The company has several similar trials underway for a range of cancers.
